title: Grief and loss
summary: When someone or something is gone — bring the sorrow to God without rushing yourself to feel fine.
graceGuardrail: Grief is not a lack of faith. Jesus wept. Tears do not disqualify you from God's love, and hurried cheerfulness is not holiness.
framing: Loss rearranges the world. This reset helps you tell the truth about the ache, receive God's nearness, invite wise company, and take one gentle next step.
why: Grief is love with nowhere to go. Scripture does not erase sorrow; it gives a God who is near to the brokenhearted and a hope that death and loss do not have the last word.

steps.title: Welcome the tears
steps.explanation: Jesus wept. God counts tears. You do not have to perform strength before you are allowed to mourn.
steps.action: Name the loss in one sentence: “I miss ___” or “I lost ___.”

steps.title: Enter God's nearness
steps.explanation: The Lord is near to the brokenhearted. Presence comes before explanation.
steps.action: Say: “You are near. Hold me in this ache.”

steps.title: Enlist wise company
steps.explanation: Weep with those who weep. Grief is lighter when someone sits with you — friend, pastor, counsellor.
steps.action: Name one safe person to tell, or write a message you can send later.

steps.title: Practice one gentle next step
steps.explanation: Blessed are those who mourn. Hope does not cancel grief; it keeps you from grieving as those without hope. Take only the next gentle step.
steps.action: Choose one gentle act: rest, a walk, a meal, a prayer, or a memory you honour out loud.

whenToUse: A relationship, job, dream, or season has ended
People expect you to “move on” before you are ready
Sorrow and faith feel hard to hold together
sixtySecond: Name the loss honestly before God.
Say: “You are near to the brokenhearted.”
Take one gentle step — rest, tell someone, or honour a memory.
prayer: Father, You see this loss. Thank You that Jesus knows tears. Hold me close, give me wise company, and walk with me one gentle step at a time. Amen.

scripture.insight: Mourning is not a spiritual failure — comfort is promised.
Hope shapes grief; it does not forbid it.

safetyNote: If grief turns into inability to function, thoughts of self-harm, or prolonged despair, seek pastoral and professional help promptly. If you are in crisis, get emergency support now.
